caption:
Thank You, Club Soccer 💙⚽

After all the practices, games, wins, losses, laughs, and tears — this chapter is closing, and my heart is so full. Club soccer gave me more than I ever imagined. It gave me lifelong friends, unforgettable memories, and lessons I’ll carry forever.

To my teammates: thank you for becoming family.
To my coaches: thank you for believing in me and pushing me.
To my family: thank you for every drive, every cheer, and every sacrifice.
And to my Pop in heaven — I played every game with you in my heart. I hope I made you proud. 💙

This game shaped me, and this journey will always be a part of me. But now it’s time for bigger and better things- see you soon Ann Arbor 〽️
#ClubSoccerForever #ThankYou #GratefulHeart #ForYouGrandpa

caption:
Surgery wasn’t part of the plan I had for myself, but I know it’s part of the plan God wrote long before I ever stepped on the field. This journey has tested me physically, mentally, and spiritually but I’ve learned that even in pain, God is working. Sometimes He has to slow us down to remind us where our strength truly comes from.

I won’t pretend it’s easy. Watching something you love get put on hold hurts. But I also know that every setback is setting me up for a stronger comeback. I’m ready to put in the work, to stay patient, and to trust His timing every step of the way. Playing D1 soccer has always been a dream, and that dream hasn’t changed if anything, it’s only burning brighter.

So here’s to faith, healing, and hard work. Here’s to trusting that God’s plan is bigger than my pain. And here’s to the comeback that’s already in motion. All glory to Him for giving me the strength to fight for what I love. ❤️❤️

never thought i would be saying this, but here i am. life works in mysterious ways, but this i just couldn’t process to understand why me. but, why not me? God has given me this obstacle to challenge me and teach me how to be a better human even without the one thing i’ve always loved. soccer. I will be guided and taught how to preserve by the presence of God by my side. I’m grateful to have all that I do in my life and will take each day as it comes. i will be back❤️

I believe in myself, I can do this and I will. 

❤️‍🩹

caption:
This is for the little girl who had a dream. 

A dream she thought was crazy, a dream she was told was too far fetched for someone from a small town with a small program. And despite all that, went for it anyways!

I had a dream of going to Paris 2024 since  2017 after competing in the Canada Summer Games, 1 year after starting in the sport of rowing. I knew it wouldn’t be an easy path and would take many long hard years of work, of living away from my family to train, never being home for a summer, and never ‘living like a kid’ as I had to be up at 5am to go to practice. But if you’re going to dream - dream big. 

I put up these pieces of paper on my wall in front of my bed while going through the training and selection process to make team Manitoba for the Canada Summer Games, to remind myself of what I wanted to achieve. My dream was the first thing I saw when I opened eyes every morning, and the last thing I saw before going to sleep. 

To all the little girls and boys out there who want to try something new - DO IT!

If you have a dream - CHASE IT!

Dream big - get excited- then DREAM EVEN BIGGER!

You can do anything you put your mind to!

📸: @benedict_tufnell

#parisolympics #dream #teamcanada #rowingcanada #olympics

The I’Marion Stewart Foundation, in partnership with the Friends of Kenwood Academy (FOKA), and The Athlete Collective, we  would like to extend our deepest gratitude for the overwhelming support shown during our Thanksgiving Turkey & Food Drive this Sunday.

In the midst of the challenges so many families are facing during these times, your generosity made it possible for us to provide a warm meal, and love to the community. Because of you, I’Marion was able to bless over 500 families with a Thanksgiving meal.

This impact was only possible first by the grace of God, and through the many helping hands who stood with I’Marion in service.

To the staff of Kenwood Academy High School, Principal Karen Calloway, the front office team, the Athletic Director, coaches, clubs, golf players, volleyball team, football players, families, friends and the countless volunteers who showed up ready to work with purpose, we Thank you.
Your kindness, compassion, time and willingness to support others is what will always make moments like these unforgettable and worth it all.

This is what community looks like. This is what love in action feels like.

Just know,because of your support, and contributions, more families will enjoy a warm meal and feel the care of a community that stands with them this Thanksgiving season.

From the depths of our hearts,

caption:
The future starts on the field.
On May 31st, we’re turning Bolingbrook into a breeding ground for greatness.
The 1st Annual I’Marion Stewart Youth Football Camp is officially locked in — powered by the I’Marion Stewart Foundation and hosted at BHS Football Stadium.

Young athletes ages 6–17 will get a chance to level up with:
	•	Developmental drills
	•	1-on-1 matchups
	•	Camp gear + food provided
	•	Vendors & giveaways
	•	And a chance to earn the MVP award from none other than I’Marion Stewart, with special guests Greg Newsome (CB, Browns) & Jayden Reed (WR, Packers) pulling up.

This isn’t just a camp. It’s a movement to uplift the next generation and show them what’s possible — right here in their own city.

Spots are limited. Let’s build something bigger than football.

caption:
That’s all she wrote.

As I have finally hung up the cleats, I have the opportunity to reflect on the past 17 years of playing the greatest sport ever invented. Football has grown me into a man in a way that is impossible to replicate elsewhere in life, and for that I will always be grateful. 

If you know me, you know how much time and energy I devoted to being the best that I can be at this game. In hindsight, I can confidently say I gave this game everything I had in pursuit of greatness. In reflecting on my journey, I realized that what I gained from my devotion to my goals were not the outcomes that I sought when setting them. In fact, nothing will ever go exactly according to plan. Don’t expect it to. Instead, the best things I gained were the irreplicable bonds I made, and the intangible qualities that the adversity of football forced me to equip myself with.

As for the things I did accomplish, none of them would have been possible without those at RFH, Princeton, and Michigan who selflessly helped me these past 17 years. The biggest thank you belongs to my family/loved ones who built the best support system I could have ever asked for without asking anything in return. I will always be indebted to these people. As I recently told someone, it’s real easy to do what I’ve done when you’ve had the people that I’ve had. 

I wouldn’t change a single thing about my career. I’ve donated a lot of blood, bones, ligaments, muscle fibers, and maybe a few brain cells to this sport. And I would do it all over again if I could. It is a privilege to have been a part of something worth sacrificing for, and not everyone is fortunate enough to experience something like that. 

Now some guys—and maybe even myself at one point—think life is all about football. It’s not. But for me, football was a hell of a way to get the most out of life. 

(I put as many pictures from over the years as Instagram would allow)

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a knack for clutch catches, this tight end combines agility and strength, embodying a relentless work ethic. Off the field, his infectious enthusiasm uplifts teammates.

caption:
Those who stay… will be champions
Those who are champions… live forever

I am scheduling this post on January 2nd and thinking about how crazy this next 2 weeks is about to be. I am so grateful for this last year, specifically to my Coaches Family and Friends, you have made this last year the best I could have imagined. Hopefully by the time this posts, which is the during my surgery, I have chosen to come back to Michigan. I also hope that in these next 2 weeks I don’t lose too many of my people to the portal or coaching carousel. God is great and I know his will won’t be altered from any decision that I or any of my teammates make. Ann Arbor is a special place, regardless of who is here. Michigan is the same, today, tomorrow and always. Go Blue forever.

Update… it is January 12th… I’m staying at Michigan, Go Blue

caption:
The ironic tragedy is that life has to be lived forward but only makes sense in reverse. 

I recently suffered a tear in my ACL and LCL in my right knee. Through conversations with my family and the coaching staff, I have decided to pursue the necessary surgery to get it fixed and endure the long recovery process. This means an unexpected end for my senior season. 

My heart is broken and it tears me apart knowing that I cannot go and do what I love. Lucky for me I have an unreal support system that I know will always have my back. The plan is to just take everything day by day. 

Amor Fati

caption:
I’m a bit late on this post. However, I’m incredibly grateful to have graduated from the University of Michigan with my degree in Biomolecular Science. This journey was anything but easy; filled with late-night study sessions, highs and lows, and countless internal battles. But through it all, I kept putting one foot in front of the other. I truly wouldn’t be here without the unwavering support of my family, friends, and coaches; thank you for always believing in me. Most importantly, I thank God for the gifts, the challenges, and the strength to persevere. He never gave up on me, even when I wanted to give up on myself.

I’m excited for what’s next. Onward and upward!

caption: I’ve always told myself that my identity isn’t solely in wrestling but when you fall short of something you know you’re capable of achieving, it truly tests your faith. This weekend didn’t bring the result I was hoping for, and I’d be lying if I said it doesn’t hurt. But there’s something miraculous about the joy God provides when you realign your focus on Him; a joy that surpasses all understanding, lifts your head high, and mends even the deepest parts of your heart. I’m truly grateful for the experiences and opportunities God has given me. Now, it’s time to move onward and upward. (Philippians 3:13-14)

my lovely Nana, 
my bestfriend and my favorite person!!!!! What a wonderful life you lived… all while being the most unconditionally-loving grandmother ❤️

Thank you for holding my hand and making me feel like the most special girl in the entire world. I feel so lucky to have gotten 21 years living right down the road from you and a relationship like no other. I always looked forward to Octobers knowing you were coming home from Harbor Springs and we would get endless sleepovers together. If you know me, you knew Nana… and anyone who knew Nana absolutely adored her.

Until we meet again… I already miss you more than words can say. I couldn’t be happier knowing you’ve reunited with Christ and are at peace 😇

caption:
Had the opportunity to volunteer and help raise funds for ART:DIS at the @art.dis.singapore Charity Golf Event 2024 at Tanah Merah Country Club last week! Thank you to @alau3111 and @bravolifestylegolf for having me to be a part of the ART:DIS community. I met many new people and wanted to thank every one of you who donated for a good cause at my novelty hole. We managed to raise quite a sum and I would like to thank you all for making this event a successful one! 🙏

*ART:DIS is a leading non-profit organisation dedicated to create learning and lifelihood opportunities for persons with disabilities in the arts. ART:DIS aims to work with allies to find universal solutions that organises society in a way where disability inclusion is the norm. They are therefore committed to changing physical, attitudinal and communication barriers whilst increasing access so that their students and artists with disabilities can participate actively and equally in society. More donations are welcome!🤗

caption:
Singapore Ladies Masters 2023 🌸

T46 - 72,76,75

Made my first cut in a professional event and couldn’t have been happier to have done it in Singapore at one of my favourite courses!! ❤️

To be able to compete with such great players on the CLPGA Tour was such an honour and I am so grateful for this opportunity. Thank you to LLD Sports, Auntie @lyn_yeo and @lagunanationalgolfresortclub for organising, hosting and giving me the opportunity to compete in this prestigious event. I learnt a lot from the pros I played with and know that I have to work harder to reach the next level as there are still some parts of my game that is lacking.

Shoutout to my dad for caddying for both my sister and I, thanks for putting up with us this week! 🥰

Lastly, huge congrats to @shannon_so_tan for the big win! So proud of ya 🫶🏼

athlete.name: Caylie McMahon
athlete.bio: This agile guardian thrives under pressure, showcasing relentless determination and sharp instincts. With a fierce competitive spirit and an infectious enthusiasm, she turns every match into a display of resilience and teamwork.

caption:
We are so excited and incredibly honored to announce that we’re running the 2026 Boston Marathon for Spaulding Rehabilitation’s Race for Rehab team, raising funds for a cause that means the world to us.

On March 12th, 2021, Caylie underwent emergency surgery to remove a tumor from her spine and woke up unable to move her legs. At just 18, she was told she would never walk again. She was transported to Spaulding where her recovery journey began. With the support of extraordinary therapists, she progressed from a wheelchair, to a walker, to a cane, and ultimately walked out of Spaulding’s doors far sooner than anyone expected arriving at the University of Michigan for field hockey preseason that August. She went on to have an amazing five-year career at Michigan that just finished up. Lindsey has been by her side through it all, playing together since fifth grade at Northeast Elite and later as teammates at the University of Michigan.

Our connection to Spaulding began even earlier through our coach and mentor, Chelsey Bettencourt, who rebuilt her life there after a rare spinal stroke in 2015. Her strength became a guiding light during Caylie’s own recovery.

Now, five years after being told she may never run again, Caylie is taking on the Boston Marathon with Lindsey still by her side. We are running in honor of Caylie, Chelsey, and every person who has found their strength through Spaulding.

Donate and read more about our story through the link in our bios. Every dollar raised supports Spaulding’s programs, therapies, and research that help patients recover and redefine what’s possible. Thank you so much for your support, whether through a donation, sharing our story, or cheering us on from Hopkinton to Boston we are so grateful!!

caption:
HISTORY MADE 🇺🇸 

It’s taken me a while to find the right words to describe this experience and this team. Although it wasn’t the finish we wanted or could have achieved, this team still was able to finish with the highest ranking ever by a U.S. Woman’s team in indoor hockey. From ranked 28th to 7th in the world in just a few years. It is always an honor to have the opportunity to represent the U.S. This time was such a special honor to wear the captains band for my country. 

The girls on this team hold such a special spot in my heart. The memories and laughs we shared together will forever be with me. Over the years whether it was walking with lions, slipping down icy mountains, watching sunsets, or winning and losing games, I never stopped smiling and laughing with this group. My forever best friends. 

For all of these amazing opportunities, friendships, and memories I have to thank Jun and Richard. All they have done for the USA  indoor program is something that cannot be matched. They have allowed this form of the game to flourish and grow. It has been an absolute honor to play for them both, and I cannot thank them enough. 

The future of USA Indoor is unknown, but I hope to continue to be a part of this special program, keep this special form of hockey alive in the states, and continue to make history. Go states!

caption:
🏑💙 Meet the Engaged Athlete Fellows!

Today, we’re spotlighting Claire Taylor, a student-athlete on the University of Michigan’s Field Hockey team.
For Claire, being an Engaged Athlete means using her voice and platform to positively impact the community around her—empowering kids to get involved in sports while learning how to become confident, compassionate leaders. She believes athletics can be a powerful tool for growth, connection, and civic responsibility.

Through her project, Athletes for Access, Claire is working to increase civic engagement by addressing inequities in youth sports across Ann Arbor, Ypsilanti, and Saline. By hosting free clinics led by Michigan student-athletes, the initiative introduces K–8 students to new sports while teaching teamwork and collaboration. Older students also gain insight into how athletic skills can open doors to college scholarships and higher-level participation. By combining athletic mentorship with civic education, Athletes for Access creates meaningful spaces where sports and community empowerment come together—on and off the field. 🌟🏑✨

Swipe to learn more about Claire’s impactful work! ➡️

The same hallways where her father once trained now echo with the rhythm of Zoë Bormet’s cleats. In Ann Arbor, Michigan, legacy is not abstract; it is something students can feel under their feet as they follow the same paths that earlier generations walked. In this episode, I interview Michigan catcher Noah Miller, who shares insights about his experiences in college baseball, including his time in the Cape Cod League, the challenges of balancing academics and athletics, and the importance of mental preparation. We then discuss the significance of teamwork, the role of analytics in game preparation, and his personal goals for the upcoming season. Lastly, Noah emphasizes the need for discipline, accountability, and a growth mindset in achieving success both on and off the field. Thank you for joining the podcast Noah!

The podcast can be listened to by clicking the link in the pages bio

caption:
🌊🏀 Spotlight: Ashley Sofilkanich x
#FoguthAthlete

Meet Ashley Sofilkanich, Michigan women’s basketball forward and one of our incredible FFG partnership athletes.

In this video, Ashley opens up about her journey, from transferring from Bucknell to Michigan with the goal of leading the Wolverines to a Final Four. She also shares her vision of her dream retirement. Living by the Jersey Shore and enjoying life on her boat. She also reflects on what Peace and Purpose for your Money means to her.

At FFG, we’re proud to partner with athletes like Ashley who are building their futures with intention, integrity, and confidence. The same way we help our clients plan for theirs. 💙✨

About Ashley:
Ashley Sofilkanich is a 6’3” forward from South Amboy, New Jersey, now in her junior season at Michigan. A standout transfer from Bucknell, she earned Patriot League Player of the Year honors, averaging 19.7 points and 8.4 rebounds per game. Known for her power inside and academic excellence, Ashley brings both talent and discipline to the Wolverines’ frontcourt.

#FoguthFinancial #PeaceAndPurpose #ProudMichPartner

caption:
10/30/2010 🤍🤍

Today is always a significant day to the Byars family . Many people don’t know that we had the chance of losing our mother at an early age. 14 years ago today, she was rushed to the ICU with a ruptured double brain aneurysm. One inside the brain and the other behind her eye. Which was terrifying because most people don’t survive. By God’s grace she’s here today with the same smile, love and beautiful soul. Someone who’s always willing to do for others and never herself. I can’t imagine life without you and all of us being the people we are today. In times where my faith withers I always come back to you. Not only your faith, strength and perseverance but how you managed to remain the greatest person ever. You’re the rock in our lives and we love you so much. The definition of a walking testimony. Enjoy your day because it’s all about you. 
 #brainaneurysmsurvivor #strongestwomaniknow

Jr. All-Star athlete. Future Wolverine. Certified bucket.  Get to know @mcke25ie off the hardwood. ⭐️⤵️   Q: Who is your favorite WNBA player? A: Favorite WNBA player would be Kelsey Plum.

Q: Why did you choose your jersey number (#25)? A: Because it was my mom’s number in college, and my first number I ever wore.

Q: What are you most excited about going to Michigan next season? A: Being able to create new relationships with my teammates and coaches!

Q: What is the most played song on your playlist right now? A: Second Chances - Kiana Ledé

Q: What’s your favorite basketball memory? A: Winning the ESPN championship at Run4Roses after being down 20.

Q: Who has been the biggest inspiration or most influential person throughout your basketball journey? A: My mom, she’s always put me in positions to succeed and taught me what a good work ethic should look like!

Q: What’s your favorite hoodie in your signature collection? A: My favorite hoodie is the black Hustle> Hate!!

caption:
We are born to live. From the moment we are thrown into the universe, we breathe, eat, drink, procreate. It is what we do as living organisms. But why would one procreate, let alone find a reason to stay alive, without something to stay alive for?
We as humans don't stay alive for the sake of survival , but rather for things that bring purpose; religion, art, music, love. in a endless oblivion of darkness and space, humans are the only species primitive enough to care, You must do what you love.
The best things in life will always end in conflict, that is why we humans are primitive.

caption:
This summer I had the chance to help design something I wish I had as a Nike Elite athlete myself — a mentorship program built by and for the next Nike Elite generations.

For one year per class, the Nike Elite Near-Peer Program connects former Nike Elite athletes with current ones, creating space for real conversations about sport, growth, and life beyond competition. Our team of mentors are part of some of the best sports programs in the country including the University of Texas, University of Georgia, Stanford, and of course, the University of Michigan〽️!

Honored to help launch this with the support of the NSAF and Nike helping along the way!

Onto outdoor 🙏🏼🙏🏼❤️… Creased my shoe for the last pic but it was worth😂

caption:
Dear Roncalli Volleyball,

This program has given me more than I ever could’ve dreamed of. If I tried to talk about everything it’s done for me, this caption would go way past the limit, so I’ll keep it short and sweet.

Thank you for shaping me into not only a better volleyball player, but a better person. Four years ago, I never would’ve believed I’d end up at Roncalli, and if you would have told me I’d gain a family, collect memories that’ll last forever, win a bunch of trophies, hang banners, and even win two state rings, I’d laugh. 

To my teammates—thank you for the endless love, laughter, and motivation every single day. You’ve all left a mark on me, and our bond and sisterhood will always be something I cherish.

To Coach Raz and Coach Bell—thank you for being the best bonus moms a player could ask for. You believed in me even when I didn’t believe in myself and always showed me love no matter what.

Roncalli Volleyball, you’ve completely changed my life. You’ve taught me that my worth isn’t found in my performance, but in who I am and who I play for. I’ll forever be grateful for this program and everything it’s given me.

I’ve dreaded this goodbye for years, and I can’t believe it’s finally here. #12 out❤️💙

caption:
We’re thrilled to announce Madeleine Scarth as ZIYNX’s Athlete of the Month for July!

Madeleine isn’t just making waves, she’s creating whirlpools of excellence both in and out of the water. A standout sophomore at the University of Michigan, Madeleine is a fierce competitor on the women’s water polo team. She’s earned her spot on the 2025 Canadian Junior World Team, representing her country on the global stage with pride and power. But her drive doesn’t stop at the pool’s edge. 

In the classroom, Madeleine is equally impressive. She’s pursuing a double major in Political Science and French, showcasing her dedication to both intellectual and cultural growth. She brings the same level of intensity and passion that fuels her athletic performance.

Madeleine’s relentless pursuit of excellence, on every front, exemplifies what it means to be a ZIYNX athlete!

caption:
SENIOR SZN ✅
I want to start off by saying how grateful I am to have had the opportunity to meet so many amazing people and travel the world throughout my junior career. I can’t thank enough my coaches, family members, friends and anyone I’ve met along the way who has supported me and guided me. I would not be in the position I am without these people.
Unfortunately my senior season did not come to an end in the way I’d hoped. Throughout the season I had been dealing with various shoulder issues constantly trying to balance recovery with preparing for competitions. Day 1 at nationals unfortunately took everything out of my shoulder as I’d reached the limit of pushing through without causing any more damage. Taking into account the much bigger goals I have in the future I made the decision to scratch Day 2 of nationals. Nonetheless I’ll be forever grateful for both the highs and lows within this sport.

“No man ever steps in the same river twice, for it’s not the same river and he’s not the same man”

I’ll be back.

caption: Day 2! Today started from 6:30 am and ended at 8 pm. I explored multiple museums. I learnt more about bloody Sunday. The 8 million Black people incarcerated during slavery. The different state laws. And so much more. I share this video because I want to inspire those around me to take an opportunity like this. My name is displayed on the screen because I vowed to NEVER stop speaking about what happened in Alabama and what my people went through all over the world. #big10lifeofseries #selma @bigten @umichwsoccer enjoy this edit 😇

athlete.name: I'Marion Stewart
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with an eye for opportunity, this wide receiver blends agility and precision, dazzling fans with acrobatic catches. Off the field, a charismatic leader and dedicated teammate.

caption:
First and foremost I would like to thank God for giving me this opportunity and ability to do what I love. 
I would like to thank every head coach, position coach, and recruiting staff from each University. I appreciate the time each of you put into recruiting me, making sure my family enjoyed each visit, and for the time you took away from your family to spend with me and mine.

I’Shawn, my big bro thank you for the laying the foundation, thank you for always making sure I’m good, making time for training or whatever I have needed, being one of my biggest fan and my inspiration. I’ve been chasing greatness since I could remember, I was determined because of you. I love you Twin

To my POPS! Man you have made this ride LITTY, all these years and I’m glad I had you on my left or my right, rather we was in a car or had to take flight. I appreciate you, I always have appreciated being able to look and see you had made your way on a sideline lol, enjoyed it all! I love you man! Last and definitely not least, my Queen behind the scene that makes it all possible. Ma you have prayed me through, cheered me through, hugged me, cried and laughed me through all my life. I don’t know how, but Somehow you make everyone in your life feel like they #1, and I know I’ve definitely acted like a middle child. Just want you to know I love you so much and appreciate you and my pops for all you done, always showing up, have sacrificed and continue to do to make sure we chase our dreams and work on our goals.

To my entire family and friends, thank you for all the support, and all the love!

Thank you to all the guys that have went on and put on for the Midwest. 

With all that being said

I am will be a student athlete attending THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN for the next 3-4 years.〽️

Time to work〽️

This is exactly why we started Loom. To give back. To make health and wellness something our youth can see, feel, and believe in. Because when they have the right tools, they can do anything.

Now we’re calling everybody in — parents, coaches, mentors, big bros and big sis energy. Let’s build up the next generation together. Healthy, strong, and locked in.

This movement’s for them — and it starts with us.
And to everyone who’s been rocking with us — thank you. We see you, and we appreciate the love. 🙏🏾❤️

caption:
This was my path to wrestling in college. I speak about some of the major obstacles. It was never a steady path, and it continues to be unsteady, but that's to be expected

The common cliche is, "progress isn't linear", but it's a cliche for a reason: It's true. Obstacles are inevitable, and reaching goals in the face of adversity is the standard. 

Although reaching these goals can be incredibly satisfying, it is important to remember that you will spend more time training and working than you'll spend winning matches. The bulk of your character comes from training and not from the outcome. 

Enjoy that process.

NUNCA DESISTA DOS SEUS SONHOS! 🥹✨

A @sbalduccini começou a nadar ainda criança no Clube Paineiras do Morumby... e o resto é história! 🏊‍♀️

Ela participou dos Jogos Olímpicos de Tóquio, em 2020, se tornando, aos 16 anos, a nadadora brasileira mais jovem em olimpíadas desde 1980, competindo no revezamento 4×100m livre! 🤯

Além disso, ela participou também das Olimpíadas de 2024, conquistou medalhas nos Jogos Pan-Americanos Santiago 2023, Jogos Pan-Americanos Júnior Assunção 2025 e foi a primeira brasileira a subir ao pódio do NCAA Divisão I em prova individual (bronze nos 200 m livre representando a University of Michigan). 😮‍💨

caption:
The ‘drop and catch’ exercise is a critical tool for sprinters. This plyometric drill involves dropping a weight, catching it quickly, and exploding upwards with maximum force.

This trains your nervous system to generate force rapidly, and the ability to be explosive for faster acceleration and top speeds in sprinting.

Reactive strength is the ability to quickly produce force in response to a stimulus—is essential for sprinters.

Adding drop and catch exercises to your training routine can significantly improve your sprinting performance. This dynamic drill helps with explosive starts and maintaining high velocity, perfecting the skills required to excel in your sport.

Try incorporating drop and catch exercises and notice the improvement in your performance 

Some ways to incorporate drop catch in your workout:
- Drop and Catch Bench Press
- Reactive dept push up 

#physiotherapy #strength #swimmer #performance

caption:
Catching “Chaos” Drill

🥇 In my opinion, this is the best drill to help translate your training to the game and make your training more game-like

🔑 for younger players, this can help them create quicker catch-block decisions; for older players, this will help them find a  secondary stance that they can block, catch, and throw from and do all of it at a high level

⚙️ make this drill hard; call “runner” at various times; make sure you are always securing the ball after blocks; this drill will help you turn up the intensity and not get too sped up during games

✅ as seen in the video, one adjustment I have made is going from a “sprinter stance to kick out” secondary stance to a hybrid (somewhat kicked out) stance to kicking back into a sprinter stance during steal attempts (essentially flipping the methods); I often found myself in situations last year where I wasn’t in a good stance to throw; this drill helps a ton with that, as seen

this drill was introduced to me by my highschool catching trainers, @tgelly and @caruson13 , but is also a huge staple of what we do at @umichbaseball @andrewstone3

caption:
Everyone runs for a reason.

For me, running is all of that and more. It’s taught me discipline, resilience, and the importance of showing up  day in and day out. 

So, why do I run? Because it makes me better: physically, mentally, and emotionally. It’s about being better than you were yesterday and being the best version of yourself. 

Now it’s your turn: Why do you run? Drop your reason in the comments.

caption:
Today, I wanted to share a bit about my own journey. 

To show you that even though I’ve progressed, I started out just where you are. 

In picture 1 I was just running for fun and the love for competition. I wasn’t very consistent in training since I was primarily a hockey player. 

So next time you look at an athletes page and wish you looked like them, or could run as fast as them....

Remember that we all have a start point. 

We are all a beginner somewhere along the line. 

But you have to embrace that process, embrace the consistency and embrace the small, daily habits that lead to big results. 

Sometimes, your progress will slow, but it’s those who consistently work hard that see long term results.

caption:
Mental strength isn’t just about pushing through. It’s about being real….

Meet Joseph Oyebog Jr. — a Michigan 🎾 commit, former top 15 recruit for the class of 2029, top 150 in the world, and someone who’s still figuring things out one step at a time.

“Tennis has tested me in ways I never expected. Many people see me and my career so far and would think I’ve had it easy, but I’ve faced burnout — not just from training and travel, but from the pressure I put on myself to be great all the time.

There were days I felt like I couldn’t meet my own expectations, let alone everyone else’s. What helped was learning to slow down. Taking breaks. Writing. Meditating. And reminding myself why I fell in love with tennis in the first place.

One of the hardest moments was coming back from injury when everyone expected me to bounce back instantly. I wasn’t ready. But I showed up anyway — and I learned that mental strength doesn’t always mean pushing harder. Sometimes it means listening to your body and giving yourself grace.

I’ve definitely felt the pressure to appear mentally tough. But that’s not real toughness. Real toughness is being real with yourself, even when it’s messy.

This is my story, and I hope it inspires even just one person to not be afraid to take care of themselves mentally.”

@josephoyebogjr

Forehand In-N-Out Drill with @maxexsted 🎾🔥

This is a simple yet highly effective feeding drill to work on both your inside in, and inside out forehands out of the add side. Below are a few tips on executing this drill ⬇️⬇️⬇️

1. Footwork: Make sure to recover to the center after each shot. Next, allow your right leg to swing behind you to allow fluid movement into the shot.

2. Margins: Try to aim a few feet inside the lines. This allows for a safer target while still producing a great ball.
